review_notes:
I read all 75 lines of the target file. I also read the upstream file SpectralOverlapPaths.lean, which defines spectralPathDensity, spectralGroupPath and spectralGroupDiagonal and states the nonnegativity, integrability and monotonicity facts for them. I searched the InvariantIsing tree for uses of `intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval` and checked its signature in Mathlib, along with `Set.monotone_projIcc`.

Two proofs in the target file run the same argument, and the upstream file runs it twice more: `spectralGroupPath_monotone` and `spectralGroupPath_le_diagonal`. The argument is that the primitive r ↦ ∫ 0..r of the density only grows on [0,1], combining nonnegativity, integrability on [0,y] and monotonicity in the interval. CavityFieldPath.lean already factors exactly this argument out for a different density (`cavityFieldPrimitive_mono`), so there is precedent in the codebase.

Other proofs I considered and rejected:
- `_nonneg` is a single API call.
- `continuous_cavityCanonicalCoordinate` uses its argument only once.
- `_at_path` is routine unfolding.
- `cavityCanonicalLabel` and `continuous_cavityCanonicalLabel` are thin wrappers.

Uncertainty: I could not compile anything, so the proposed rewrites are untested. They rely on two definitional unfoldings: that `spectralGroupDiagonal` is defeq to `∫ r in 0..1, …`, and that the subtype `≤` coming from `Set.monotone_projIcc` is defeq to `≤` on the coerced values. Either step might need an explicit `show` or `Subtype.coe_le_coe`.

findings.problem: Both proofs re-derive the same fact by hand: for 0 ≤ x ≤ y ≤ 1, ∫ 0..x of the spectral density is at most ∫ 0..y of it. Each one builds its own `integral_mono_interval` call from three pieces: the bound x ≥ 0, an `Eventually.of_forall (spectralPathDensity_nonneg …)` witness, and a `spectralPathDensity_intervalIntegrable … ⟨_, _⟩` witness for [0,y]. `_monotone` also re-proves monotonicity of `projIcc` by hand with `max_le_max le_rfl (min_le_min le_rfl hst)`, which is exactly the body of Mathlib's `Set.monotone_projIcc`. The same four-part call appears twice more upstream, in `spectralGroupPath_monotone` and `spectralGroupPath_le_diagonal`. That makes four copies of the same reasoning, differing only in where x and y come from.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one helper to SpectralOverlapPaths.lean, which the target already imports:

theorem spectralPathDensity_integral_mono (ρ eig : ι → ℝ) (hρ : ∀ a, 0 < ρ a)
    (hρsum : ∑ a, ρ a = 1) (p : OverlapPath) (a : ι) {x y : ℝ}
    (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hxy : x ≤ y) (hy : y ≤ 1) :
    ∫ r in 0..x, spectralPathDensity ρ eig hρ hρsum p a r ≤
      ∫ r in 0..y, spectralPathDensity ρ eig hρ hρsum p a r :=
  intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval le_rfl hx hxy
    (Eventually.of_forall (spectralPathDensity_nonneg ρ eig hρ hρsum p a))
    (spectralPathDensity_intervalIntegrable ρ eig hρ hρsum p a ⟨hx.trans hxy, hy⟩)

Proof sketch: this is the existing four-part call, stated once with x and y as parameters. The two target proofs then become the following (untested):

lemma cavityCanonicalCoordinate_le_diagonal … :=
  spectralPathDensity_integral_mono ρ eig hρ hρsum p a
    (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one t).property.1 (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one t).property.2 le_rfl

lemma cavityCanonicalCoordinate_monotone … :=
  fun s t hst => spectralPathDensity_integral_mono ρ eig hρ hρsum p a
    (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one s).property.1 (Set.monotone_projIcc zero_le_one hst)
    (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one t).property.2

The upstream proofs collapse the same way. `spectralGroupPath_monotone` becomes `… (p.nonneg s) (p.monotone hst) (p.le_one t)`, and `spectralGroupPath_le_diagonal` becomes `… (p.nonneg s) (p.le_one s) le_rfl`. The hypotheses are unchanged, because every caller already has 0 ≤ x, x ≤ y and y ≤ 1 available.
findings.benefit: The monotonicity of the density's primitive on [0,1] gets one name and one proof instead of four copies spread over two files. Each proof that uses it shrinks to a single line that says which interval endpoints are compared, and the hand-written `max_le_max`/`min_le_min` step is replaced by the Mathlib lemma. If the integrability or nonnegativity API for `spectralPathDensity` changes later, for example to an a.e. hypothesis or to a new integrability domain, only the helper needs updating. Readers also see directly that `_le_diagonal` is just the y = 1 case of `_monotone`.
